intent: Provide an offline, self-contained recovery tool that repairs a stale EFI System Partition from the systemd emergency shell, and prevent the failure recurring by gating kernel transactions on a mounted ESP.
scope: Non-goal: no network access at any point; recovery uses only /var/cache/pacman/pkg
Non-goal: does not source linux_configuration/scripts/lib/common.sh - the tool must stand alone in an emergency shell
changes: boot-repair: detects and repairs the 2026-07-30 emergency-mode failure chain - stale ESP kernel, gutted module tree, unloadable vfat, unmounted ESP, missing modules.dep, shadow kernel files written into the root filesystem's /boot, noauto/nofail fstab drift, and ParallelDownloads > 1 (the alpm-hook segfault trigger that was the root cause).
Treats a module tree as usable only when BOTH vmlinuz and kernel/ exist, so the metadata-only wreckage the bug leaves behind is never selected as the target kernel.
Safety guards on the only destructive path: files under /boot are deleted only while it is not a mountpoint AND contains no EFI/ or loader/. EFI/ and loader/ are never written or removed.
Recovers vfat offline by extracting fs/fat + fs/nls from the cached kernel package, since mounting the ESP requires the very module the failed upgrade deleted.
05-boot-mounted-guard.hook: PreTransaction gate with AbortOnFail that refuses a kernel install when the ESP is unmounted.
99-boot-autorepair.hook: PostTransaction auto-repair that fixes ESP drift before the machine is ever rebooted, exiting non-zero if it cannot.
--root flag makes the logic testable against fixture trees and usable from an Arch ISO chroot.
install.sh verifies its dependencies, installs to /usr/local/sbin (root filesystem - the ESP is unreachable when this is needed), and runs the installed copy to prove it works.

verification.evidence: 31 passed, 0 failed. Covers healthy system, stale ESP kernel detect+repair, gutted-tree rejection, newest-complete selection, fstab noauto/nofail reset with backup, shadow-file deletion, the refuse-to-delete-a-real-ESP guard, ParallelDownloads fix, missing modules.dep, no-kernel guidance, CLI contract.

11 passed, 0 failed on the real machine. Unmounted the real ESP, confirmed the preflight gate opens when mounted and closes when not, confirmed dry-run writes nothing, planted shadow files and confirmed they were deleted and the ESP then mounted with EFI/, loader/ and kernel 7.1.5-arch1-2 intact. EXIT trap remounts the ESP regardless of outcome.

(1/3) Verifying the ESP is mounted before installing a kernel... boot-repair: ESP mounted at /boot - proceeding. (6/6) Verifying the ESP received the new kernel... Both hooks fired; post-transaction hook silent, meaning nothing needed repair.

==> boot-repair: ABORTING TRANSACTION / error: failed to commit transaction (failed to run transaction hooks) / Errors occurred, no packages were upgraded. Nothing was written into the unmounted /boot. The gate held.
Clean. SC2034/SC2155/SC2115/SC2001 fixed at source rather than suppressed.
Clean, matching the options used by scripts/meta/shell_check.sh.

risks: The PreTransaction hook uses AbortOnFail, so a bug in boot-repair --preflight would block all kernel upgrades. Mitigated by the live test proving both the open and closed paths, and by --preflight being a single findmnt check.

The 99-boot-autorepair hook is itself forked by alpm, so it is subject to the same ParallelDownloads segfault it compensates for. This is why boot-repair also enforces ParallelDownloads = 1 rather than relying on the hook alone.
Shadow-file deletion is destructive. Guarded by requiring /boot to be unmounted AND free of EFI/ and loader/; both guards are covered by fixture and live tests.
If the running kernel's package is absent from /var/cache/pacman/pkg, vfat cannot be restored offline. The script reports this and prints Arch ISO chroot recovery steps instead of guessing.
rollback: After rollback validate that a kernel transaction still completes: sudo pacman -U /var/cache/pacman/pkg/linux-*.pkg.tar.zst, then confirm findmnt /boot shows the ESP and the version in /boot/vmlinuz-linux has a matching /usr/lib/modules/<ver>/ directory.
